answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a bond in a vault and earn access through randomly selected, cross-checked tasks. A new agent’s claims are compared with a mirror record of prior behavior, while inconsistent answers trigger slashing and exclusion. Creating many identities therefore does not create instant influence: the attacker must fund every bond, perform costly work, and risk losing deposits when random audits sample the dune of fake agents.
